audit.whatIsWrong: The stored chart (Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir, Skill, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir) contradicts every prose field on the same page. whys[0] says Overload out-ranges you at 1; whys[1] and whys[2] say 2 and 3 are 'even'/'skill'; whys[3] and the mid paragraph say level 4 tips to Ryze. The packet levelChart agrees with the prose: Ryze, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir.
audit.why: Three independent sources (packet chart, whys[], mid paragraph) agree against the four stored rows, so the rows are the defect.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 become Ryze, Skill, Skill, Ryze. Rows 4-6 already read Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir and are correct.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ryze's level-4 spike is described as a 'Flux spread' with no mechanism or numbers, and Realm Warp is correctly called a non-duel spike but no cooldown is given anywhere.
audit.why: Spell Flux is a 615-range single-target debuff on 3.5s falling to 2.5s; Overload is 1000 range on a flat 5s and is reset by every other basic ability. Realm Warp is 180/160/140s at 3000 range and grants no combat power.
audit.corrected: The spike is Spell Flux enabling the W root and the Overload reset chain, not a passive 'spread'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page treats Rune Prison as an unconditional 'point-blank root'. Riot's own text: Rune Prison damages and SLOWS; it roots only if the target already has Flux on them. Vladimir's answer therefore is dodging Spell Flux (E), which the page never mentions.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it is absent. Without Flux there is no lockdown, so Ryze cannot land the follow-up combo.
audit.corrected: Dodge Spell Flux (E, 615 range) and Rune Prison is a slow, not a root. Rune Prison is 11s at rank 1 down to 9s at rank 5; Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1, so bait W before you spend the pool.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison: matchup-defining — His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rune Prison: 11s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5, and it only ROOTS if Spell Flux (E) landed first — unfluxed it is just a slow, so dodge the E and the lockdown never happens. - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1. - Hemoplague: 120s, kill windows only.

edits.before: His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Rune Prison only roots if Spell Flux (E) hit you first — dodge the E and W is just a slow.

edits.before: Ryze wastes Rune Prison — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Bait W with a step-up, then commit — Pool is 28s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Ryze's Rune Prison: His point-blank root — sets up his combo. Bait it. When it is down — Q-drain, pool his answer.
edits.after: Rune Prison roots only through Spell Flux (E); unfluxed it is a slow. Dodge E and his 615-range combo has no lockdown.

edits.before: Ryze's Overload (Q) plus Rune Prison (W) root chains huge poke; his level 4 point in E for the Flux spread lets him double-Q you hard.
edits.after: Ryze's Overload (Q) is a 1000-range line on 5s, reset by every other cast; Spell Flux (E) at 615 is what makes W root instead of slow.

notes: MIRROR CONFLICT — do not silently trust either side. The ryze-side audit recorded the chart as 'Vladimir, Skill, Skill, Vladimir, Ryze, Ryze, Vladimir', which is close to a name-swap of the packet chart (Ryze, Skill, Skill, Ryze, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir). Row winners are absolute names, not side-relative, so a swap looks like the ryze agent inverted them the way ratings invert. I went with the packet chart because both whys[] and the mid/late paragraphs on this page independently agree with it. Also unverified and left alone: spikes[3] and the late paragraph call Sanguine Pool 'pool immunity' that 'dodges his root windows' — 2s untargetability is in the kit, but whether it clears an already-applied root is not in Riot's text.
